Trying to be fair , it was the evening of Sunday after Longchamp races, but that should not have come as a surprise to the restaurant, we were told 30 min wait which turned in to 40 not real issue. Then we were shown to a table and watched the staff run round like headless chickens without a drink or menu for 30mins then we ordered 2 cold starters and 2 rump steaks with french fries. After a further 25 mins (still no drink) we asked if there was a problem with the starter, a further 5 mins saw the definitely ordinary starters arrive. After that it turned into a circus, the well done steak was raw, sent back and was then still raw, it was sent back and was still running blood. The french fries never arrived so we paid the bill begrudgingly and left the food and the restaurant without any sign of remorse from the staff. While we were being treat appallingly the staff were very attentive to other guests . Do not use this restaurant because unless you are french you will be treated as second class.customer...

After strolling along the canal (and watching all the canoeing going on there), we popped into O.kay Cafe for a crepe and a drink. We sat in the outside area, with a good view of the canal. The staff were friendly enough, the crepes were tasty (though quite salty) and the drinks were cold.

Emplacement d'enfer, vraiment ! Nourriture et service archi-pourris. Vraiment un gros gâchis pour cet établissement qui, géré par des gens passionnés et futés pourrait vraiment devenir un truc top et sympa. Au lieu de ça, ambiance exécrable et humeur détestable des serveurs qui en ont peut être marre de servir des plats insipides et froids, dans un lieu sans déco et sans âme... En attendant que ça change, allez manger au Draco juste à coté ; on y trouve une carte cohérente, un chef cuisiner, des serveurs pros et sympas et une atmosphère (déco en autres choses) vraiment chaleureuse. Tout ce qui manque au OK café qui n'a pour lui qu'un emplacement exceptionnel absolument sous exploité.

Très belle terrasse, agréable en été. L'hiver il y a également une vue appréciable sur le bassin de La Villette. La nourriture est bonne (crèpes, salades...), assez simple et bon marché. Le service pourrait être un peu plus agréable.

Quel Plaisir (oui avec un grand P) de prendre une grenadine dans ce café en fin de journée ensoleillée le week-end. L'ambiance très simple du lieu détonne avec la vue de la terrasse : un panorama magnifique sur le canal de l'Ourcq. On ne fait que parler du 25° Est, mais en terme de quiétude et de vue, je vote largement pour celui-ci. Le personnel est sympathique et bon enfant, ils n'ont pas pris le melon malgré le fait qu'ils détiennent selon moi l'une des plus belles terrasses de Paris - et ça ne gâche rien au plaisir.

A deux pas du métro Marcadet-Poissonniers, à l'angle de la rue Marcadet et de la rue Simart, "Au Fond du Bar" vous accueillera dans une ambiance chaleureuse de bistrot parisien. Profitez en famille ou entre amis, tous les dimanches et jours fériés d'un brunch tout en simplicité et convivialité. Le personnel vous guidera dans la découverte du buffet varié proposé à volonté. On vous invitera à goûter au smoothie maison du dimanche tout en dégustant des plats simples de qualité à base de produits frais. De la confiture au fromage, en passant par les boissons chaudes et froides, et les jus de fruit, les classiques sont là, voir un peu plus. Les petits gourmands comme les grands trouveront leur bonheur salé ou sucré avec le choix de tartes, salades, crêpes, gâteaux, viennoiseries, compotes et autres délicieuses idées du Chef. Ne manquez pas l'assiette bacon et pommes de terre sautées accompagnée de sa verrine d'oeufs brouillés et de son gratin de choufleur ! Un parfait moment de détente et de dégustation dans un cadre simple et discret et un personnel à votre écoute. Lancé depuis peu, ce charmant brunch a déjà ses habitués et on comprend pourquoi. N'hésitez pas à revenir, le choix de tartes, salades et autres plats changeant au grè des saisons !

Deuxième jour des Soldes, nous commençons toujours par un "crème" mon épouse et moi, sortant du bus près de Notre-Dame et nous dirigeant vers St-Germain, nous sommes tombés sur cet établissement qui sentait bon le café... Parlons donc du café.... Une tuerie de chez "Coutûme".... On y a pris deux très beaux et très bons crèmes (Latte), le service est un peu long , le nouveau Barman/Barrista est en formation, mais très sympa... La déco du lieu est minimaliste, new style typée Manhattan, franchement Bobo Hype... Par contre tout y est soigné, propre et de bon goût. Les toilettes étaient nickel et j'ai beaucoup aimé la déco du couloir et le grand miroir lorsqu'on se lave les mains. En bref, nous y avons été bien accueillis, bien servis, dans un décor sympa, et les prix du crème valent largement ceux des autres (2 fois 4€, mais là ils étaient délicieux...). On a beaucoup apprécié.

ATTENTION A NE SURTOUT PAS CHOISIR !! PIEGE A C** J'ai eu l'occasion de découvrir Loulou's Diner à l'occasion de l'anniversaire d'un ami, je n'ai jamais eu une aussi mauvaise expérience. La cuisine est plus que passable, des hamburgers comme on en fait partout, l'hygiène déplorable (trouvé : un cheveu dans ledit hamburger) mais le pire est encore le service. A l'arrivée, nous sommes (groupe de 10) reçus comme des malpropres placés au sous-sol où on nous oublie plus de 15 minutes durant. A la réception de la commande la serveuse se permet même de nous refuser certain plat. Au moment de payer clou du spectacle : elle vient demander une première fois 10€ (soit-disant manquants) à une personne, puis une autre. Au total c'est 20€ de volés !

Pour les amateurs de burgers, je vous conseille de tester Loulou's Friendly Diner près de Cluny la Sorbonne. Les burgers y sont vraiment délicieux, le pain est fait par Eric Kayser, les frites sont présentées dans des petits paniers de friteuses, ce qui est assez original. Le cadre est agréable et cozy, il y a des fauteuils pour les plus chanceux. Ils font également des brunchs, à tester !

Cuisinés par Phillippe labbé, chef étoilé et mondialement connu, les brunchs du Bauhinia Restaurant vous propose un cadre exceptionnel des mets de qualité, à l'inspiration asiatique. Proposés tous les week-end de 12h00 à 15h00 (malheureusement non disponible du 21 Juillet au 19 Août), les brunchs de cet établissement sont divers et variés. Voici un petit aperçu de ce qui vous sera proposé au Bauhinia : - Guacamole à la crème de wazabi et pomme Granny Smith, - Jambon artisanal de Trevelez , rosette, ou chorizo - Emincé de bœuf mariné au citron vert - Piment à la mode thaïe, Salade Yam Som de crevettes, concombre, papaye verte, mangue et ananas Makis concombre et avocat/saumon, Rouleaux de printemps aux légumes et tourteaux - Œufs au plat, à la coque, pochés, brouillés, en omelette... avec un choix de 2 garnitures, - Oeufs bénédictine à la truffe noire - Thé ou chocolat chaud fondu à l'ancienne - Jus de fruits pressés - Buffet de desserts. Et encore beaucoup de surprises du Chef doublement étoilé au guide Michelin.

Here is one the places recently opened in Paris that I wanted to test by all means! It was a nice suprise when I found out this lovely venue in north Marais, ideal for those looking for food that is not only healthy but also truly good. Guess what? This is another veggie café – following the so popular 'healthy food' trend – nicely decorated with girly-style, perfectly suited for girls as all the dishes served are gluten-free, 100% organic, 100% homemade. However, the core concept may also please men: a new style of food which is both healthy and delicious. I went there for Sunday brunch, which I found super good, freshly prepared, originally composed, particularly tasty – but slightly overpriced. Victim of its success, Café Pinson is often crowded, especially during the week-ends. By chance I called last minute and got a table for two immediately, but rather be ready to queue for a while.

Mon expérience au café pinson : - Une attente sans fin pour nos assiettes. Une amie a demandé à être servie rapidement car elle n'avait rien mangé de la journée et se sentait mal, réaction ? Des gens arrivés après nous ont été servis avant elle. - Si vous avez faim, n'y allez pas. Les plats sont très peu copieux, et les entrées sont une simple (très simple) mise en bouche. Avec tout ça, et pour couronner le tout, un prix exorbitant pour la qualité de la prestation.

Ambiance basque pour ce brunch. Deux formules vous sont proposées : la formule classique à 20,50€ et la formule basque à 25,50€, le tout sur une base de buffet sucré / salé (assortiment de desserts, de quiches salées, salades composées, cakes salés, etc.) et fruits pressés. Les boissons chaudes sont également à volonté ! A côté du buffet, une assiette salée vous sera servie composée de : pilons de poulet, saumon mariné, pommes sautées, coleslaw et oeufs brouillés pour la formule classique, ou bien de produits basque pour la formule basque avec : axoa de veau, riz gaxuxa, fromage basque, saumon mariné, oeufs brouillés au piment d'espelette, gâteau basque et sa confiture de cerises noires. Pour déguster tout cela, ne manquez la grande table d'hôte à l'intérieur, avec au plafond l'incontournable drapeau régional. Pour les amateurs de rugby, prévoyez de venir ici un jour de match, vous pourrez suivre les plus belles rencontres l'après-midi après votre brunch.

I have eaten pizza at Pizza Pino for at least 25 years. The pizza is consistently good, but is a bit more expensive than other places. I can't attest to the quality of the other food, but the pizza is made on-site, and I like it. Pizza Pino is one of the few pizzerias that's open all night, so it's a place to go when getting back from a trip or from working very late. As others have noted, the service is slow, because the restaurant is always busy. The pizzas here (and almost everywhere else in France) are designed to be eaten by one person. The pizza will fill your plate. Don't expect to share a few pizzas, because we don't do that in France. Also, the pizzas doesn't come sliced, so you'll need your knife and fork (Something to keep in mind if you come with small children). Pizza Pino has take-out, but I have always eaten on-site.

After a queue of 20 minutes in a late saturday afternoon, we were so happy to enter the temple of hot chocolate :) very pricy (9€ the hot chocolate served with a little pot of whipped cream) but that's an experience that is worth living for the breakfast of for tea time, and especially during winter at least once ! Ask to be sitted up stairs if possible, cause the main room is super noisy and not really cosy.

Something of a Paris institution, Angelina is a grand Salon du Thé which exudes class at every step. It's been serving locals and visitors alike with exquisite patisserie, artery-clogging hot chocolate and fine coffee since 1903. Angelina is not cheap, but you are paying for the quality and it's definitely worth a visit. Although it has an extensive food menu, for me there's only one reason for visiting Angelina: its signature patisserie, Le Mont Blanc. This is a rich concoction of whipped cream on a meringue base, encased in chestnut cream vermicelli. Divine! The perfect accompaniment is Angelina's amazing hot chocolate, l'Africain, which is incredibly rich and smooth. However, if that's not to your taste, there are many other fine offerings on the menu and the coffee's pretty good too! And, of course, there's the pleasure of sitting in the beautiful salon itself... A word of caution though: Angelina is very popular and you are very unlikely to get in without having to queue, sometimes for quite a while. If you don't fancy the wait, there is a takeaway counter where you can get the main items from the patisserie menu, including the Mont Blanc.

Not to be missed. This gorgeous, old fashioned tea room serves up some of the best hot chocolate in the world. Rich and creamy, with the optional chantilly cream on the side, it's served up in silver pots and poured into elegant teacups. The place is perfect for people watching, as despite the heavy tourist presence, the French ladies who lunch still come to sit, chat and read their papers. Tiny perfect sandwiches and pastries are the perfect accoutrements to your gluttonous afternoon tea. I'd skip lunch first ;)

Want to enjoy a real hot chocolate or some delicious pasteries? Then have a stop at Angelina. Oh you can't miss it, if you play your cards right you'll be enjoying those right into the Louvre! That's some fancy panorama most places can only dream of. Sure you pay the price for it, but it's well worth it.

Somehow we managed to arrive after visiting Louvre with almost no line at all. The atmosphere is great and takes you back to the beginning of 20-th century. The hot chocolate was great, and so was the "Choc African". We liked the "Le Mont Blanc" less than I've seen in reviews, but it was good. The service is slow, but the stuff is very friendly and speak English.

Le PSG attend ce moment depuis décembre dernier : les huitièmes de finale de la Ligue des Champions. Après avoir creusé l'écart en championnat, les Parisiens peuvent pleinement se concentrer sur Valence. 

« Paris est évidemment favoris »
De leur côté, les joueurs valenciens redoutent cette rencontre face au PSG. « Ils font désormais partie des gros d'Europe. C'est vraiment une équipe qu'il faut respecter » a confié Tino Costa en conférence de presse. « Evidemment ils sont favoris » a lâché Ernesto Valverde, l'entraineur de Valence avant de reprendre « Ils ont terminé à la première place de leur groupe ». Les Parisiens ont en effet impressionnés lors de la phase de poule, alors que le club espagnol a lutté pour arracher la deuxième place de son groupe.

« Pas seulement Ibrahimovic »
Valence, pourtant habitué à la Ligue des Champions, craint notamment l'armada parisienne : « Paris, c'est plus qu'Ibrahimovic. Il n'y a pas de plan spécial pour le contrer. C'est toute l'équipe qu'il faudra arrêter » prévient l'ancien montpelliérain. Même son de cloche pour le coach espagnol : « Paris, c'est comme le Real Madrid. C'est une équipe qui joue en contre, avec beaucoup de puissance devant et des latéraux qui montent souvent ». Le PSG fait d'ailleurs partie des équipes les plus prolifiques en attaque avec quatorze buts inscrits en six rencontres.

« Une carte à jouer »
Même si les hommes de Valverde se positionnent en tant qu'outsider, les Espagnols comptent bien saisir leur chance face au PSG : « La motivation est évidemment là. L'ambiance sera bouillante. Nous sommes en bonne forme mais surtout nous vivons pour jouer ce genre de rencontres face à ce genre d'équipes. Le monde entier va nous regarder » s'enthousiasme l'entraineur de Valence. « On connaît nos qualités. Nous avons plus confiance en nous depuis quelques semaines. Nous avons une belle carte à jouer » averti quant à lui Tino Costa.

Les joueurs du PSG sont donc prévenus. Même favoris, les Parisiens devront prendre au sérieux cette équipe de Valence, sous peine de se faire piéger

Grand favori du championnat, le PSG a enfin pris quelques distances avec ses rivaux. Jusque-là, le club de la capitale avait occupé seul le fauteuil de leader uniquement lors de la 10e journée avec un petit point d’avance sur Lyon. Il en a désormais trois de plus que l’OL et six que Marseille. De quoi briser leurs ambitions? « Ça a été un super week-end… pour le PSG, reconnaît Joey Barton, le milieu anglais de l’OM. 
SUR LE MÊME SUJET
Beckham étrenne sa nouvelle tenue« Ceux qui jouaient moins ont lâché »
Paris, Lyon, Marseille : trois leaders au cribleLigue 1 : un nouveau match à trois commence Mais on regarde toujours vers l’avant. »

Un PSG inarrêtable 
Meilleure attaque, meilleure défense, Paris n’a plus perdu en L1 depuis le 1er décembre à Nice (1-2). Même laborieux en janvier, Paris a engrangé sept points. Les voyants semblent tous au vert. « Il s’est passé un truc, confirme Olivier Rouyer, consultant sur Canal +. Lyon et Marseille ont des absences inquiétantes. Paris, en revanche, dégage une grande sérénité collective. Ils sont passés au-dessus des autres et cela risque de s’accentuer. » « Je ne crois pas que le championnat soit plié, coupe Eric Di Meco, consultant pour BeIN Sport. Paris peut aussi avoir encore des soucis. Ils vont devoir gérer les matchs autour de la Ligue des champions. »

Lyon et Marseille dans une mauvaise passe 
Le début de l’année 2013 a coûté cher aux deux rivaux du PSG, alors que les trois équipes étaient encore à égalité à la trêve. En moins d’un mois, l’OL a laissé échapper cinq points et Bastos, l’OM a perdu Rémy tout en voyant huit points s’envoler. « On a dit plusieurs fois que Marseille était mort, note Eric Di Meco. L’OM est une équipe à réaction capable de perdre contre n’importe qui mais qui peut également gagner face à tout le monde. Lyon, de son côté, a certes des trous d’air mais ils sont plutôt réguliers depuis le début de la saison. Il ne faut pas tirer d’enseignements trop hâtifs. »

Fin du suspense dans un mois? 
Le 10 mars, l’OL reçoit l’OM. Deux semaines plus tôt, les Marseillais se seront rendus à Paris. Une double confrontation qui devrait permettre de cerner l’issue du championnat. « Lyon et Marseille auront une énorme pression car ils n’auront plus de droit à l’erreur sur ces matchs », prévient Vincent Guérin, l’ancien milieu parisien. « Contre Lyon, ce sera un tournant de la saison, confirme Barton. Mais le PSG reste le favori logique. » Les rivaux de Paris semblent d’ailleurs déjà un peu résignés. « Je pense que le PSG dispute un autre championnat que le nôtre, estime Rémi Garde, l’entraîneur lyonnais. On s’efforce de rester accrochés le plus longtemps possible, mais il ne faut pas regarder seulement devant. Notre objectif, c’est le podium. » Cela ressemble presque à une abdication…

Riding the line between "sparse decor" chic and actual shabbiness, this is a great place to sidle up to the bar for a good glass of off-the-beaten-path wine and a bite to eat. Even for a small plates menu, options are haphazard and the skill behind each dish varies greatly. Fare is good but not worth a long trip, so unless you're already in the 11th, there are better versions of the stripped down, small-plates wine bar thing elsewhere.

I had the pleasure of dining at Au Passage for lunch last week at a friend's suggestion. I was very pleasantly surprised ! The restaurant is located on a small street (Passage St Sébastien) in the 11th and not one that you would stumble across by accident so make the effort to visit it. It was not very busy when we arrived but filled up in no time before we left. The lunch menu is limited to 1 appetizer and a choice between 2 main courses followed by either cheese or dessert. We started off with a wonderful trout that was done in a gravlax style followed by delectable fish with fresh vegetables and a touch of mint (nice addition). We finished with the perfect piece of cheese. The service was generally very prompt and pleasant. The restaurant had the charm of an old bar or diner with a combination of regular tables and chairs mixed with lower tables, sofas and comfy arm chairs. In the background, Elvis was playing which brought a smile to my face :) The evening has a larger choice and it is a tapas style menu (please note that there is not much if you are vegetarian) and I am looking forward to trying their evening fare. The price is extremely affordable and worth every Euro !! If it is anything like the delicious food served at night, it will definitely be my reason to visit the 11th more often !

Un resto à tapas de qualité absolument délicieux. Anchois au piment d'Espelette, rillettes maison, mulet en escabèche, bonite, encornets... tout est fait maison. Ne cherchez pas de passage couvert, mais plutôt une petite rue dans laquelle se niche ce resto bon vivant. Déco rétro / brocante, plats à partager façon tapas et petits vins bien choisis. Les ingrédients sont simples mais de qualité. Pensez à réserver car l'endroit est victime de son succès, et le service un peu débordé les soirs d'affluence. Comptez 3 tapas salés par personne, à environ 10 Euros pièce. Au final l'addition peut monter, mais l'on y passe un bon moment entre amis.

Malgré un prix important (prix quasi unique de 10€/tapas) il y est impossible de manger à sa faim car les assiettes ne sont vraiment pas remplies. En plus, la faim est attisée par le fait que les tapas sont servies au compte-goutte : il faut compter pas moins de 20 minutes entre chaque tapas pourtant commandées en même temps ! La cuisine est bonne mais sans plus (Plusieurs des tapas commandées baignaient littéralement dans l'huile !). Après 21h30 les deux tiers de la quinzaine de tapas de la carte ne sont plus disponibles (j'avais commandé avant, ouf ! Mais il y avait la queue dehors..). Le personnel, manifestement surchargé est absent (oubliée, j'ai du réitérer ma commande de vin) et assez désagréable ; en sortant des toilettes, sans s'excuser, une serveuse qui se précipitait vers la cuisine voisine m'a bousculé en commençant à me pousser de son chemin. Bref, dans ce quartier on peut facilement trouver mieux pour moins cher ‼

Testé ce dimanche midi, j'ai apprécié ce restaurant dans la plus pure tradition française. L'espace est grand, haut de plafond, bien éclairé, le mobilier est en bois avec glaces et dorures... c'est cossu ! Ça pétille de mille feu et on s'y sent bien. Ici, on fait forcément la part belle à la viande de bœuf. Les plats sont copieux, vous êtes assurés de prendre votre part de protéines pour la semaine. :) Le service est très professionnel. On ressent le respect de la cuisine comme du client. Bref, ce "Boeuf Couronné" est une adresse sure qui vaut le détour dans le quartier de Villette.

J'ai fait le Boeuf Couronné un dimanche midi en famille, et je dois dire que pour ce genre de restaurant, cela collait parfaitement ! Le cadre est authentique, avec une salle à l'étage assez chic (sans être luxe) On est confortablement assis, sur de grandes tables. Grand est d'ailleurs un adjectif qui revient régulièrement au Boeuf Couronné. Les pièces de viande servies sont très généreuses (on est là pour ça après tout) et les couteaux pour la couper sont "king-size" ! J'ai testé le pavé de Chateaubriant à partager et ses quelques 750 grammes : un must avec une cuisson de l'ordre de l'impeccable. Le personnel est au petit soin, ce qui vient renforcer le sentiment de bien être que l'on ressent dans ce restaurant. On est là pour bien manger et le repas peut s'étirer pour grignoter sur l'après midi dominical. Un très bon moment. Prévoyez tout de même un bon budget, car au risque d'enfoncer une porte ouverte : manger de la bonne viande, ça coûte cher .

Meilleur restaurant à ma connaissance : un excellent menu à 34€ tout compris qui en vaudrait 50 ou plus ailleurs, viande de qualité, service agréable et efficace, décor agréable et on a de la place !! Je recommande.

Exceptional coffee, exceptional brunch. IN PARIS?!?!? This is for Emperor Norton: Brunch? In Paris? WAIT WAAaaait.... diversity in selection, for *BRUNCH*, in PARIS? Served in a coffee house that has depth, consistency, and stellar coffee. But what Emperor Norton is doing would be precarious if it wasn't so well executed. Paris is not known for Brunch, but one must start somewhere, and while many look at purveyors of new concepts as daring or risky, sometimes someone is just prescient, and dialed into trends. I think Emperor Norton saw a need, and beat the curve on a new trend. It will give them the time needed to improve upon their excellent skills and menu. I imagine they will only end up more in demand, and likely move to a bigger spot in the future. As I understand, the kitchen is not the most expansive or efficient. Any other reviewers problems might be due, in large part, to their restrictions with the setup. Coutume cafe should be happy to have them as long as possible. Emperor Norton evolves traditional breakfast fare, by adding subtle touches to some egg dishes, while creating absolutely foreign concepts for the city - like a breakfast burrito, or scrambled eggs and salsa on chips, etc. It's wonderful to enter a place and be completely surprised by the menu - it was unexpected, and completely refreshing. It was a welcome change from the traditional fare... and a marked departure from the carboloaded breakfast we are used to. This is by no means a pretentious fine dining experience - this is a modern take on CA Fresh Mexican diner morning food. They are producing tastes that are not uncommon to some of the best breakfast joints throughout the west coast of the US. The food is exceptional, the coffee is EPIC (see previous Coutume review), and it's something we can't wait to return to... not just to eat again, but to see how they grow and evolve. This is the start of something very rare, fun, exceptional in Paris, and I can't wait to see how these innovators lead the way. This is for Coutume: Is this from an American viewpoint? Yes. I love France. It's epic. The only thing I couldn't get the hang of was ordering "café". I usually got an espresso, etc. I don't know what I was doing wrong, but I was with french speakers the whole time. An iced coffee ended up espresso on ice. It's all good... I dig that I am a cultural immigrant. I was patient. Then I came to Coutume. Stellar service - kind, patient, and professional. They suffered my Americanism with grace and class. They also excel at coffee in a way few places in Paris understand. Multiple types of brewing, shockingly good foaming.... I don't need to ramble on to make the point: This is 5 star coffee in a city with 2 star options for hot caffeine. The post dinner espresso is ubiquitous, but anything else is trouble to find. Coutume produces such quality coffee, I greedily had so much I was vibrating my surroundings for about 6 hours. Expertly brewed, expertly served, and delicious. It's a demur, unpretentious place.... but an exceptional treat nonetheless. We wouldn't have found it if it weren't for Emperor Norton, so I would consider their brunch team a big help in getting the word out about this exceptional coffee house. THANK YOU!

Situé en face du métro Alexandre Dumas, le café d'Albert est une brasserie typiquement parisienne décorée par Yannick Cinelli dans les tons baroques et contemporains, avec une terrasse très agréable. L'accueil est chaleureux et le service très correct. Le brunch vous est proposé sous la forme d'un buffet au prix de 23€ comprenant pour la partie froide : salades de riz, salades de pâtes, plateau de viandes froides, oeufs durs, charcuterie, salade de concombres, salade d'haricots verts et un plateau de fromages. Pour la partie chaude, vous aurez le choix parmi: oeufs brouillés, saumon, quiches, saucisses de volaille, saucisses de porc, pilons de poulet, bricks à la brandade de morue, verrines de crevettes. Après le salé laissons la place au sucré avec également des verrines à la vanille, de la salade de fruits, des corn-flakes, viennoiseries, du fromage blanc, des tartes et gâteaux maison. Côté boisson : jus d'orange, café, thé, chocolat, lait chaud ou froid. Un brunch complet pour bien démarrer la semaine.

Tout est démesuré dans ce lieu. De l'accueil au service, des plats au vins en passant par le décor et les tarifs. Mais aller dans un de ces très grands restaurants parisien, c'est entrer dans une autre dimension, toucher, l'espace de quelques heures, l'intouchable, le sublime, la perfection. Il faudrait que le Michelin créé une catégorie spécifique pour ce type d'établissement tant ils sont (doit y en avoir 4 ou 5 en France) au dessus du lot. Sur les 8 plats proposés, 4 sont sublimes et mettent littéralement le cerveau en pause tant la richesse des goût est intense, les 4 autres « simplement » grandioses. Bravo à toute l'équipe pour son professionnalisme haut de gamme sans être guindé.

Un bar super cool!! Bien situe dans paris, dans une ambiance jeune et energique, un pub des plus branches qui redonne toujours le sourire avec un personel tres sympa, toujours a l'ecoute et jamais desagreable!

Bar bien sympathique qui ferme assez tard, le service est rapide et agréable, la musique et l'ambiance sont vraiment biens. En revanche les boissons (aux prix corrects pour un pub parisien) ont assez fréquemment un goût très bof (un mojito à la poubelle, un pastis immonde…). Mais bon si on est pas trop regardant et qu'on veut danser jusqu'à tard c'est la bonne adresse d'autant plus qu'il est plutôt bien situé !

L'ambiance est vraiment pub, du coup, allez y pour la bière parce que les cocktails ne sont pas tous au niveau de leur prix. Après, faites vous plaisir sur les pintes tout au fil de la soirée qui peut se finir assez tard. Mais attention, plus ca dure, plus l'addition fera mal.

As an American, I'm not used to high prices and small portions but the service was fantastic. This restaurant has a rich history of Hemingway and Sartre. The wine selection was outstanding and we loved the wine that the server recommended. We ordered the sea bass with vegetables, which was simple in taste. The duck with mashed potatoes was so tender that I didn't even think it was duck. The lamb was outstanding and came with vegetables. The medium sirloin steak was medium rare by American standards and very enjoyable and comes with mashed potatoes. All the meats came with a sauce on the side that was delicious. The ambiance was the best part. As we were eating dinner, we were entertained by live opera singers and violinists in the park nearby.

Café de Flore is a grand café in the old style, dating back to 1885. Popular with tourists and locals alike, it is, for me, part of something quintessentially Parisian, the stereo-typical grand café par excellence, complete with waist-coated waiters. The coffee is good and there's a range of food from breakfast through lunch to dinner, along with a range of pastries. If coffee's not your thing, there's tea, hot chocolate, soft drinks and a very impressive array of drinks from the bar. The only potential downside is the price: for a city with a reputation for being on the expensive side, expect to pay twice as much in Café de Flore as you would elsewhere in Paris. Of course, you're paying for the experience and that little touch of class, which, for me, is well worth it!

Aurais-je du comprendre retour du client ou du plat ? Pour les planches, c'est assez correct (ancienne expérience). Mais pour le tradi - Manger quoi ! -, évitez les terrines industrielles de lapin, lièvre, cerf, sanglier et porc servies avec du beurre (... et oui !) et dont le seul mérite est de ne pas se cacher au service à 9,5 € sur la carte contre 3 € au supermarché du coin.... Oubliez vite aussi le bourguignon de viande bouillie chaud dessous-froid dessus micro ondé et servi sans aucun autre accompagnement qu'une sauce improbable genre Knorr et ce au tarif de 13 € !!! Last weekend my wife and I spent in Paris were fantastic and Le Fumoir contributed to make it special. We had a brunch Sunday morning, the place was busy but the waiting time was about 10 mins (the advantage of being just the two of us helped skip the queue a bit). The atmosphere in the restaurant is warm and cozy, from the windows on the left handside you can enjoy the view of Saint Germain Church (which I suggest to visit right after lunch). Service was quick enough and very kind, the actual cost of the brunch seemed to me ridiculous: only 24€ per person and it included a soft drink (juice), tea or coffee, a main course (I had an amazing scrambled eggs with toast and smoked salmon), dessert, different types of bread (from sweet to savoury) and a home made marmelade. I strongly suggest to visit the place because it is good, nice, good value, right behind the Louvre and besides Saint Germain Church as I mentioned before.

A very small and romantic bistro off the beaten path Le Petit Troquet. The most difficult part of the evening will be finding it. Rue Expostion is a small alleyway off the Rue Saint-Dominique adjacent to Les Fables de La Fontaine. Rue Saint-Dominque is the home of Christian Constant's empire.. Upon arrival you will be greeted by the Chef/Owner's girlfriend that is the manager and server in the dining room. The ownership has changed this year and if you have been there in the past you may be pleasantly surprised by the new owner. The menu changes daily and has something to please everyone. I would not recommend the place for children or large parties. This is great for date night or perhaps two couples.

Recommended by our hotel as well as by Rick Steeves, this very small restaurant did not live up to expectations, at least in terms of the food, which was mediocre. The small room is charming, and the staff very friendly. All the customers looked like foreign tourists, usually a good sign that you wont write home about the food. The wine list is relatively small but the prices are most reasonable. The prix fixe menu offers a few choices of traditional dishes and each dish comes well presented. My mushroom risotto appetizer was tasteless; my beef bourguignon, apart from being a small portion, was the worst I have ever had; and my dessert, the apple clafoutis would have been rejected by highway fast food restaurants. This is the type of place which would appeal to someone who has lost his tastebuds and only cares about the atmosphere, which is charming indeed.

Le destin a voulu que nous trouvions une place à deux pas, nous nous sommes dit avec ma fiancé pourquoi pas ? L'endroit est très élégant, la population aussi, c'est agréable aux yeux. Le placement en terrasse a été correct, il nous as fallu tout de même rentrer au fin fond de l'établissement, malgré le fait de passer devant deux employés à la langue bien pendue - et aux yeux vengeur - pour avoir la chance d'être placé. Ça n'est pas grave. Les cartes arrivent, première déception, des appellations rêveuses mais qui une fois arrivé ne font plus rêver. L'ensemble de la carte se caractérise par une carte vieille france, de souche : soupe a l'oignon, escargot, viande, etc. Les plats sont dans la moyenne. C'est idéal lors d'une sortie de boite, ou par exemple ici du musée ou de la comédie française. Évidemment c'est un bistrot donc on ne s'attend pas à une restauration gastronomique mais pourquoi l'établissement, les prix et le service se veut de la haute société ? On paye au final juste le placement de ce cafe Ruc. J'ai demandé une carafe d'eau au serveur, il s'est exclamé de rire devant moi, le comble de l'impolitesse face à un client. Il faut bien comprendre qu'à 6eur le coca light et à 6,5eur le demi litre d'eau plate on préfère prendre l'eau municipale. C'est pas grave. Lors de notre diner en amoureux, on a eut la très désagréable sensation de se faire reluquer cent sept ans par le personnel. Qu'avions-nous fait ? Peut-être faisions nous tache parmi la clientèle ? Tout ça pour vous dire que seulement l'attitude des employés a été pour nous à la limite du non-respect d'autrui. Condescendance et moquerie font pas bon ménage pour un établissement de ce genre.

I had the the 'Risotto artichaut aux truffes' to start. It is a very pretty dish, with the 'risotto' separated from the top layer by a lacy layer. On top of the layer was a few little spots of artichoke mousseline, garnished with a small green leaf (beet) and a sliver of truffle. The spots of mousseline did taste like artichoke, but the risotto did not. The texture of the diced artichoke was verging on crunchy and I guess the artichoke flavour had just not developed. A serious disappointment. Overall, the dish failed (2 out 10). The wine chosen to go with it was also not the best. In my experience, a crisp sauvignon blanc or semillion SB would be a much match, given development of the flavour of the artichoke. The St Aubin, was not exciting. The next choice was Perdreau rouge (partridge). This was quite gamey as expected, but the wine match to it was a Beaune 1re cru which just did not have to strength to match the meat. I also had to watch for shot in the bird. The sauce was good, but not enough of it. A good merlot (St Emillion) would have been much better. I persevered with a cheese to follow (St Nectaire) which was a generous portion, garnished with thinly sliced mushrooms and served with a Cotes de Marmandais Lassole 2005 (8 years old). This is a predominantly Cab Franc wine and came over as heavily wooded. It blew the socks off the cheese. Even the mushroom killed the cheese. Definitely not matches. So, all in all, I came away having enjoyed the beautiful woodwork in the restaurant, but badly disappointed by the food and the alleged wine matches. I might not be able to present the food so artistically, but I can sure make a similar set of dishes that taste a whole lot better. It seems to be a place to be seen but not for really magical food.

Très beau restaurant au dernier étage de l'immeuble avec une superbe verrière nous laissant découvrir le ciel parisien. Le cadre est idéal, mais un peu bruyant (beaucoup de monde et une musique un peu forte). Le personnel est très agréable et abordable malgré un côté trop chic. La déco est signée Philippe Stark et colle parfaitement avec l'univers de Kenzo. La carte est variée et complète ; on reste en revanche sur des produits assez simples. Les plats sont malheureusement arrivés tiédis, surement à cause d'un service un peu long. Mais les saveurs sont excellentes et les produits sont bons. Les desserts sont excellents (+1 pour le Complètement Chocolat de Pierre Hermé). En revanche on ne s'étonnera pas de l'addition qui est un peu élevée, surement justifiée plus par le cadre du restaurant que par la cuisine...

Le Cannibale café, restaurant de type vieille brasserie parisienne vous accueille pour son brunch le dimanche de 12h à 17h dans un cadre au style rétro avec de hauts plafonds, de belles moulures et colonnes ; le Cannibale Café est un lieu confortable et attirant, l'ambiance y est décontractée et conviviale, idéal pour un brunch entre amis ! Le Cannibale café vous propose de choisir entre 2 assiettes : le brunch Américain ou le Brunch Norvégien. Une fois le menu choisi, vous pourrez choisir une boisson chaude parmi les 4 suivantes : café, thé, chocolat ou lait, et l'on vous apportera rapidement un jus d'orange pressé. Puis votre assiette arrive. Celle-ci est compartimentée en sucré/salé. La partie « petit-déjeuner » est identique aux deux brunchs : elle se compose de 2 mini-crêpes accompagnées de chocolat dans un petit pot à part, de fromage blanc avec du muesli, une petite brochette de fruits frais et pour finir un délicieux smoothie pomme, ananas, gingembre. Le brunch Américain se compose de la manière suivante : oeuf bénédicte au bacon, écrasé de pomme grenaille sauce ciboulette, beans (haricots) & chipolatas et Coleslaw (salade chou cru et carottes râpés, oignons) Le brunch Norvégien se compose, quant à lui de : oeuf bénédicte au Haddock, écrasé de pomme grenaille sauce norvégienne à l'aneth, lentilles en salade et carré de saumon et tomate croque au sel. En un mot, les 2 assiettes proposées sont tout aussi équilibrées, complètes que savoureuses.

Aimant la nourriture Italienne, “Les cailloux” est pour moi LE restaurant par excellence me permettant de retrouver ce petit bout d'Italie en plein Paris. Dans ce restaurant familiale, j'y retrouve tout ce que j'aime, l'accueil de la Mama comme en Italie, l'endroit chaleureux et cosy aux lumières tamisées… J'y ai dîner à plusieurs reprises et à chaque fois je me suis laissée emporter gustativement parlant. Je n'ai jamais eu rien à redire sur les plats car ils sont simplement merveilleux. Des pâtes comme on aimerait en manger tous les jours, des entrées simples & savoureuses, des plats typiquement italien, alliant fraîcheur et saveurs ainsi que des desserts qui vous laissent sans voix.

I went on Saturday June 15 to bring my parents who were in Paris for a short visit. I decided to bring them to this place because I had heard it was one of the best restaurants in Paris. This is what happened: I ordered fish while my parents ordered pork. When the fish came, I realised it was not fresh. The presentation was excellent but the taste was not good. I know it because I come from a city near the sea, and fish is the food I know the most, since I eat it everyday. After telling the waiter that the fish was not fresh, he complained and said how could I know, which stroke me because where I come from, you would never be treated this way by anybody. I tried to make him understand that I knew what I was talking about and that I wanted to change my order. Finally, the server allowed me to change the order: I ordered pork. I waited and waited for 40 minutes. My parents had already finished their meal when I asked the waiter where was the dish I had ordered. He answered: I'm sorry, but this is not a McDonald's restaurant. After that I decided the pay the bill and leave. The service manager apologised and told me the next time I came I would have a free apéritif. Needless is to say I will never go back again and that I will share my experience with everyone who asks me about that place. I was probably very unlucky. In any case, nothing is going to make my parents forget this awkward moment. It's a pity things like these happen in what could be such a pleasant city to live. By writing this review I only want to bring awareness of the fact that many servers are very agressive, non-professional and childish in Paris restaurants. If you go there, I can only wish you good luck.

Probably the nicest Brasserie in Paris and with a lot of history, a gorgeous interior, and top notch service. We thought the food was average to good, this place isn't worth the trip for the food as far as we could tell, but still a great spot over in the Bastille. Try the Il Flotante dessert, it was amazing, as were the oysters and traditionally prepared snails. Also note that they have some Alsatian food items, which I loved (german style sausage!) but my wife thought was average. Large inside but got very busy, we were there for lunch.

Stay away if you consider yourself a food oriented person. If you are a tourist that is not at all concerned with food, but want to experience a traditional brassiere, feel free... but the traditional brassiere is quite dead. As an example, it is important to understand this is tantamount to a Cheescake Factory, owned by a chain, with low quality food that is overpriced, without service to match, well, anything at all. Our meal was a disaster from start to finish. We arrived 30 min early for an 8.30p reservation. We wanted an aperitif at the bar, and arrived at 8p for that sole reason. The maitre d' insisted our table was ready, and we explained we were quite early, on our own accord, and would like to wait until our reservation time, adding that we would be happy to wait beyond 8.30p to sit in the main room under the glass dome. He said that they were fully committed, and came short of demanding we take our table 30 minutes earlier than our reservation. We were sat in a side room, upstairs, which I quite enjoyed because it was intimate and quiet, while my wife found herself feeling sequestered and second fiddle, hidden from any "experience" at all. We controlled the wine.. which seems the singular thing we could control, and were actually forced to pour our own champagne, half white, and half red bottles throughout the night. Our wines were not poured by the staff once. We got 3 courses... a) seafood plate b) onion soup c) steak tartare & traditional sausage & kraut plate a) The 6 oysters on the seafood plate were shucked, but not separated, which was surprising but easily managed. They were a bit gamey... smokey in the bad way, not the good way. The sea snails were cooked beyond overdone - they were like pencil erasers. Precisely horrid. b) my wife enjoyed her french onion soup, but I found it to be flavorless, as if made by americans - it was neither nuanced and subtle, nor bold and rich. It was like sock water, a tepid, flavorless, unseasoned almost clear broth with an absurd amount of cheese. c) the server recommended the sausage & kraut plate for my wife, which was obviously a dish that could feed 3 or 4 people. This was ridiculous for US portions... the idea that my wife could have eaten 25% of it was just dumb. It was either ignorance or a cynical upsell, but we didn't see enough of our disengaged and forgetful server to be able to make assumptions as to her service style. The sheepish smile we got with the singular disinterested check in wasn't enough to understand why it was just so bad. Chipped and broken glassware, no water refills, utterly perfunctory service in every way from door to door. My tartare was the worst I had in France, or anywhere else - it was old, warm, gummy, and flavorless. I am not sure they were meant to bring seasonings for me to do it myself, but it just was slop on a plate. The fries were rubber, as well. If it was one thing, I wouldn't have written a review at all. But after a dismissive host, forgetful service, just every single thing.... there's a certain point where people concerned with a good experience need a warning, and that's precisely what this is. I typically never write a 1 star review, and if I choose to do so it's because I want to reach the management, not other onlookers. But this isn't to management... this is to people who want a great meal and not to waste precious time while in France, or simply living life. This is a bad chain, stay away, find something more authentic and delicious. If you need a proper brassiere style meal, try Le Numero Sept (7) at 81 Avenue Bosquet. It's small, intimate, delicious, gracious, and wonderful. Everything Bofinger is not. You have been warned.

After some disappointing dining experiences in Paris (the perceived Mecca of food) we thought we would try some food from back him in Cyprus / Greece. We found Mavrommatis restaurant and it had some pretty good reviews. Our experience was phenomenal - it was the first real great dining experience in the country of France. Service was great - price were not cheap but reasonable for the calibre - food was delicious. The waiter was joking with my son and got him to eat the keftedes (meatballs) that were as delicious as my grandmother used to make them. Highly Recommended.

Cuisine grecque avec un vrai parfum d'authenticité, j'aime particulièremen la cavier d'aubergines grillées et les anchois marinés, le taram n'est pas rose barbie ce qui est toujours bon signe. Délicieuses brochettes au curcuma, très bonne qualité des produits à emporter également.

Mavrommatis proposent une cuisine fidèle aux traditions culinaires méditerranéennes et grecques tout en y apportant une touche créative en puisant dans la richesse du terroir français. Le cadre est élégant et l'ambiance feutrée avec une belle salle au décor méditérannéen, sobre et raffiné. Derrière les fourneaux, Andreas Mavrommatis concocte une cuisine fine et délicate autour de produits méditérannéens et français de qualité. L'authenticité et les saveurs de la cuisine grecque se mêlent harmonieusement avec l'utilisation de produits de notre terroir. La carte évolue au gré des saisons avec un menu tradition à 38€ (entrée, plat, dessert) et des entrées entre 14€ et 18€, des poissons entre 25€ et 32€, des viandes entre 22€ et 32€ et des fromages et desserts à 10€. La carte des vins propose une belle sélection de breuvages grecs. L'accueil est chaleureux et le service attentif et disponible pour cette table considérée comme le meilleur restaurant grec en France. La cuisine offre une belle harmonie de saveurs autour de plats légers et raffinés avec un bon rapport qualité-prix.

Etant d'origine Grec-Chypriote et étudiant à Paris, la nostalgie me prend souvent de manger un plat du pays. Mavrommatis sert des portions de bonheur à chaque fois. Je retourne au pays à travers ses plats. Si vous aimez les plats méditerranéens et frais, faites dont un tour à Mavrommatis, vous ne le regretterez pas.

We decided to eat here after reading reviews about how lovely the place was and also how average the food was. The other reviews were pretty much on track. It is a beautiful restaurant. The service was good. My Duck confit was really tasty and a bit over cooked. My wife's shrimp and scallops were terrible. The shrimp smelled really strong and spoiled. It actually made my wife gag. We are from the US Gulf Coast where shrimp are fresh. We know what shrimp should taste like. After bringing it to the attention of the server, he just stared off in space for a second and took the plate away. They did not take the shrimp/scallops of the bill. We learned a lesson. Listen to the reviews, especially the bad ones, and don't order seafood in Paris. It is a beautiful restaurant and the coffee and deserts were delicious. Just don't go for a meal. This really made for a down day for my wife.

Traditional brasserie café in Paris, not far from La Tour Eiffel but quite removed from the fake touristy feel of that area. We went for a simple lunch of steak frites and raspberry/blueberry sorbet (menu a 15 Euros) with a little Bordeaux red in a carafe. The meal was completely satisfying and well presented. When you enter the café, it's like going into a theatre, through a lobby and vestibule and then into three stories of serving space. The space used to be a fabric store, and then in 1921 became a hangout for local auto-workers. It has remained busy and popular among locals and, yes, tourists. It's a great value for the quality although it is busy and hardly intimate.

Our waiter that evening was hysterical and so professional and the food was amazing. Had such a great time. You know, if you are American (as am I) and you go to France with an attitude of American Entitlement, or expect them to be anything other than French, you will probably have a bad time. At 365 euros a person for tasting menu, L'Arpege is definitely not for everyone. The full meal runs at about 4 hours (the first 2/3 of the meal was done in about 2 hours, the remaining 1/3 took about 2 hours... so the pacing was definitely a little off for us). Since Chef Alain Passard is known for his vegetables, we came with high expectations. While he certainly pleased us with what he could do with vegetables, I was slightly disappointed to see pork and lamb on the tasting menu - though to be fair, it was probably the best lamb I've ever had and the pork was superb as well. For me, the star of the night was his cold and warm egg though. The service here was great though, they are willing to offer slightly different tasting menus for party of two so you can try out more dishes. Also, they seem to allow you to get the tasting menu while rest of your party can order a la carte.

Without a doubt the best meal I've had in my life. I had previously been to Michelin starred restaurants, but none with more than one star. L'Arpege is a world apart from those other restaurants. My wife and I had the lunch tasting menu, which was eleven courses including the amuse bouche. Each one was interesting and flavorful in their own right. The most amazing was the creamy soup topped with the smoked herring foam. Given the description, I thought I wouldn't like it at all, but it the best soup I've ever had. There were only a few low lights. The first was that our main entrees were not show stoppers. Both the lobster as well as the veal, were both very good, but not as good as some of the other courses. The second was one of the macaroons for dessert was filled with something... not sweet and was inedible. Lastly, we ordered Champagne to start the meal, which seemed nice until we saw that we were charged about 26 Euro per glass, which I think is a little steep for so-so Champagne.

cuisine correcte, endroit calme et cadre agréable toutefois, une mésaventure m'est arrivée par rapport au choix du vin, en effet méfiez-vous d'un certain serveur (plutôt maître de salle je pense, sur ticket nommé "241 Tom"). J'avais demandé une demi bouteille de Pessac Léognan 2008, à 14 € la demi-bouteille en indiquant bien sur la carte celui à 14€, n'ayant pas regardé les autres demi-bouteilles beaucoup plus chers. Le serveur est venu avec deux demi-bouteilles différentes, le Pessac de 2008 et un autre de 2009 qu'il me conseillait vivement d'ailleurs. A la fin du repas, sur l'addition, j'ai vu que le Pessac de 2009 était à 38 €... et ce coup-ci je revois la carte des vins où en effet cette demi-bouteille est à ce prix, mais par contre, il avait "oublié" de me le notifier. Je lui ai donc fais part de mon mécontentement, il est parti voir (sans garantie aucune) son directeur adjoint soi-disant pour trouver un arrangement, mais après 5 minutes, il est revenu en me disant que ça n'était pas possible, en soutenant que je lui avais demandé uniquement un Pessac, sans choix précis. Je n'ai pas été plus loin dans la discussion, en lui disant que ça devait être de ma faute, et de mon manque d'attention sur un ton totalement ironique, j'ai payé la demi-bouteille mais sur le principe, on appelle cela de la vente forcée tout de même. Donc méfiez-vous même si certains serveurs semblent très à l'aise, au point de se permettre tout et n'importe quoi. Ce n'est pas pour 34 € que je vais faire un scandale, mais sur le principe, ça mérite d'être partagé sur la toile.

Also, my wife and I tried two different flavors of Pastis (their speciality) only to find that they both tasted like 100 proof licorice, and nothing else.
Pick a starter, pick a main but whatever you do leave room for the epic all you can eat chocolate mousse, a legend in a dessert form

My entire family of 10 joined me in Paris to help celebrate by 80th birthday. I received the name of Bistrot Paul Bert from the owner of a French restaurant in Berkeley, CA, knowing I was going to Paris later that month. We walked from our hotel in the Bastille area to the Bistrot and met with the owner and told him of our plans. He made our reservations for several days later. When we arrived we were treated to a wonderful waiter, a great table, fantastic food and a birthday cake of chocolate mouse for all of us (the best individual dish any of us had in Paris). The cost was 37 euros each for a three course dinner with three great choices in each course. Our experience was the best, the food outstanding and the staff friendly (who said the French were rude?). Do go there, but do have an advanced reservation.

I was lucky to get a single seat without a reservation and left very thankful. The staff, especially the bar tender Raphael, was very kind and a lot of fun. The food was the best bistro food I've ever enjoyed - the steak was perfectly done and the frites were mighty good. (To be honest, the steak was as good as any I've had at a restaurant - including the Palm in NYC and Bones in ATL.) Worth the two trains it took for me to get there. I'll certainly be back!

The quiche of the day was ham and spinach and it was excellent. It also came with salad on the side and the dressing they used when eaten with my crepe made it sweet. It helped me finish the crepe but I didn't like it one bit. The quiche was a little on the solidified side. The egg wasn't that runny. However, they do give you a decent sized portion but I don't think the prices are worth it at this place. I wish I had tried something else but for now, I can only recommend the quiche. Giving it 3 stars not because I made a mistake in ordering but the quiche wasn't perfect and prices were high for what you got. I rarely write reviews, and I think it's the first time I find it absolutely necessary to do so. The truth about this place is that it's fashionable and "so hot right now". I'm sorry, I just can't see it. The food was good, not exceptional and definitely not worth the price we payed. But what shocked us the most is the service. It was indescribable, the worst service I've ever seen in all of the restaurants in Paris, and that's saying quite a lot. We were 4, we asked for 3 entrées and one main course, followed by 3 deserts and a reasonably priced wine. I can understand the chef not being too pleased by that, but one of the waiters actually came up to us and told us off: "That's not something to do! We're not a distraction! You're here to eat!" We had to control ourselves not to get up and leave. He kept shooting us mean looks throughout the night. COMBLE DU COMBLE, while we were talking outside after dinner, he went past on a motorcycle and had the nerve to flip us off. I'm being kind giving it two stars. Le Chateaubriand breaks the mould of only the high-end French restaurants serving haute cuisine. Whipping up wonderfully inventive food that would impress the plates of some of the swankiest venues, Chef Iñaki Aizpitarte has decided to serve his food in a simple bistro setting with a zinc bar, chalk boards and hard wooden chairs. He has made a name for himself by deconstructing some of the classic French favorites and presenting them in a new, imaginative way. All of this in a five course no-choice menu that changes daily at prices that are a total steal. Reserve in advance as the seats are always spoken for at the first service or try your luck for the no-reservation second seating starting at 9:30pm.

This isn't meant to be a bashful review, as I haven't given the establishment one star, this but simply an opinion to be considered when making your choice for dinner. We were fortunate enough to book one day in advance over the phone as it was low season (end of August, ). We were excited to eat at a restaurant ranked in the international top 50, actually ranked 18th. For those who didn't know, there is only a set menu at 60 euros or 120 euros with the wine pairings. First warning signal, there were very, very few Parisians in the restaurant and the crowd was mostly made of tourists. (we are tourists ourselves) The service was unforgettable for all the wrong reasons, e.g. rotating waiters, plates brought on the table hastily before the previous one was consumed (and we weren't eating unusually slowly), lack of knowledge of the ingredients used in the dishes (erroneous fish name, told a dish was served with a pistachio dressing when the pistachios were actually whole nuts sprinkled on the purslane), on a few occasions one particular waitress had to go back and forth between the kitchen and our table to be able list the ingredients of multiple dishes. The tostino del cielo, their signature dessert was abruptly brought on the table, presented simply with its name and the manner to eat it, after which the waiter vanished. We had to ask another waitress what the ingredients were. We had to ask for water carafe refills, the waitress then forgot and had to be gently reminded yet again. If this was a 10-15 euros meal, I could understand, but at 60? Making it more expensive than many 1 Michelin star restaurants in Paris. The food was good, not great, not spectacular. It did not provide any surprises or interesting mixtures of flavors for our palates except for the cucumber granité (part of the dessert). But as my friend sitting with me so well put it, "I did not come here for the dessert". In the end, as we asked for the bill, yet another waitress, Asian this time, came and asked in both broken French and English how the meal went and when we vocalized and gesticulated so-so, she answered with a smile and replied "good then", clearly not grasping our disbelief. She swiftly proceeded to swipe our credit card though. As a disclaimer, we are both fluent French and English speakers. Let's not mention the 4 rowdy Canadians (we are Canadian too) at the table next to us who were already well inebriated by the half-point of the courses, who were swearing and almost shouting over all the other patrons. I believe that le Chateaubriand is riding on its reputation made by the media and a few trendy blogs and reviews, cutting corners (and expenses) with its staff, yet still manages to reel in clients and making them pay the big bill for its pretty yet empty shell. What's unfortunate is how this review will be buried in the mass of overly positive reviews, most made by patrons who are lured and awed by its reputation (as we were initially) and who haven't experienced the refinement of what a 18 euros lunch or a 35 euros supper can buy. I'm glad to see that there are quite a few other patrons who took the time to vocalize their dissatisfaction and hopefully some of you will take our experiences into consideration.

Line up early for second seating, where they don't take reservations, but seat on a first come first serve basis. This attracts a number of food industry people, with it's simple, severely regressive overly informal service, and the line up at the door is always a treat. For the 8p service, line up at 7.30ish, but the line has probably gotten longer in the interim, since our visit. Maybe show up at 7p. The second service also gets a vivacious staff, brimming with excitement and energy for the night to end. Always cordial, and happy as can be.... the service falls off a cliff at one point of the evening, and you need to be direct if you want to order more wine or need anything at all. But, the food speaks for itself. The amuse bouche and inter-courses are plentiful, and wildly imaginative (w/ Bianco, 2008 - Vermentino - Sicile La Moresca). I cannot remember them all, and that is rare. They had a play on Fish & Chips (w/ Arena - Chenin - Savenniere A&R Mosse), a "Catfish, Turnip, Manzanilla" combination (Millesime 2002 - Chardonnay - Champagne J. Lassaigne). Then an Iberian pork, asparagus, green beans, and rhubarb combo (Less pezzeroles, 2010 - pinot noir - Pommard 1st Cru - Fred Cossard). It was fantastic. Every course... engaging, delicious, almost ingenious with the creativity without being polarizing. Ice Rice Cream with Prune "Bacon from Heaven" dessert.... and cheese of the day. (w/ Panesa - Palomino - Especial Fino Emilio Hidalgo) We got the menu paired with the wines (info in parentheses)... it was delicious, and a wonderful range of execution and creativity. It was a fantastic ride, but the back end service was so loose and inattentive it tainted the culinary aspect of it. We tried our damndest to order more wine, and get attention, but it was that moment in the evening where festivity took precedent over the guest. Still... a wondrous experience, and one to remember. =)

Our worst experience in France during a period of several weeks and with visits to a number of cities. This restaurant has a nice roof-top view of the Eiffel Tower -- and sat us behind the largest planter you can imagine while many, many other tables were empty. If you want to see the Eiffel Tower at night go out to the many places where there are nice views from the street -- same tower, no cost, more fun. Then go to any nearby cafe or restaurant.

If you are thinking of eating at one of the restaurants in the Eiffel Tower, you may consider dining at "Les Ombres" instead. It costs a bit more than the lower-level Eiffel Tower restaurant, but the food, service and view are better. It's also a good option for people with a fear of heights. I have been 3 times to this restaurant. Twice was it a great experience: great food, reasonable prices and freindly waiters. Just went back from the 3rd and terrible experience. We (3 persons) came at the worst hour possible (8.30PM) and were told we would have to wait at least 30 min. This was absolutely no problem, knowing beforehand it would be the case. We were served 2 nice glasses of red wine each by the very polite young bartender, together with free saucisson. After waiting a whole hour, we felt like asking the waitress if she could give us an idea how much we should wait more. VERY bad idea. She was behind the bar and had been chatting with a customer for the past 5 minutes, her back in front of the clients, when we asked with a smile the bartender, 20cm from her, "Do you think we can bother her with just a simple question?" he answered "of course, just ask her, her name's Clémentine". We turned to her: "Clémentine, please?" she turned her back and, hand on my heart, swear to God, said with the meanest face "Can't you see I'm talking here?", then turned her back,and continued "Guys interrupting women, what kind of education is that?". We were so shocked we didn't know what to say. A disappointing, symptomatic of the "Parisian waiters" way of dealing with customers followed (I'm a Parisian myself) . I won't write here all that was said but it went along of: Us "Are you kidding? We just asked a question and you're attacking us on our education, that's absolutely over the line to treat customers like this!" Clémentine: "Yeah right, i don't give a ***, that's how we do it here, come back when the Manager is here to complain, great, yeah, yeah, right" and so on... We couldn't do one thing but to leave the place, feeling sorry for the waitress but most of all for the young bartender who obviously felt bad with the scene but couldn't feel the courage to stand up for this shame of a waitress. i wish I could say "please try this restaurant, forget about the personnel, the food is worth it", but unfortunately, this being the worst experience of my life in a restaurant, I just can't.

While it also doesn't take reservations, Chez Gladines is without a doubt the best value dinner in all of Paris, so get there by 7:30 at the latest if you want a table. Based in the Butte Aux Cailles neighborhood in the 13th, it's not centrally located, but it's worth it and not hard to get to. Take ligne 6 to Corvisart and walk through the apartment corridor at the exit to find the resto at the top of the hill. Not only are most meals under 12 euros, but the plates are huge and delicious traditional Basque dishes. I always go for the Basque omelette, but the other plates are just as, if not more delicious. The Gaillac wine before and with the plat and cheese for dessert is a must.

Make sure you show up early (food service starts at 7pm, but you can start drinks around 6:30) as the place will be packed by 7:30. The waiters are very busy so the service isn't the best, but the food and good value more than makes up for it. It is a VERY noisy atmosphere, was a bit warm also in the summer. So not the best for a private meal, lots of students but we loved this place, it was the only place we would return to in Paris.

De même pour les brochettes : il y a des brochettes au coeur de poulet, foie de poulet ou coquelet ! Les portions sont assez petites et le prix élevé mais cela mérite le détour... Seul petit bémol : le service dans la salle à l'étage (nous y avons déjeuné un samedi après-midi) ; le serveur est d'une grande gentillesse, et nous sert "sans stress" (on a attendu assez longtemps pour la prise de commande) mais nous "oppresse" un peu : il fait les 100 pas dans la salle ; et nous avions à peine fini nos sashimis, qu'il nous demande si on prend un dessert/café alors que nos plateaux étaient encore sur la table. De même, l'addition est arrivée tout de suite après, sans qu'on ait eu besoin de la demander.

I work in this neighborhood and have hence gone to this bar/restaurant several times with both french and anglophone colleagues. Even though Paris desperately needs its own mircobreweries (as well as an improved selection of beer at its cafés), the beer at this one is at best extremely disappointing. If the beer is fresh, it doesn't tastes so. Furthermore, the taste is quite variable from week to week, going from barely drinkable, to not as good as a standard beer served at any other brasserie (like 1664, which isn't terribly good either). The beer is by no means "British", and if a French person tells you otherwise, it is simply because they don't know any better. Compared to a french brasserie, the ambience is somewhat anglosaxon, but to call this a British pub is being way too generous. I have never had a beer worse than this served outside of France, and I will no longer go to this establishment until they get their act together.

They forgot part of my order- then when the food was out and I asked for it, the server, who could only be described as vapid, exclaimed she was surprised i wanted my salad. When we had already gotten our food? Was I supposed to eat my salad afterwards? The pompus gentleman behind the bar was full of clever snide jokes when I asked for ketchup- and really, comedy acts for everyone should be reserved for restaurants that deliver. We left 60 euros on a lukewarm soup and the most depressing steak my husband has ever had. Please, save yourselves and go anywhere else. Paris is such a wonderful food destination- but steer far from castiglione- a poor excuse for not only French cuisine, but edible food in general.

Venus s'installer avec des collègues en terrasse en début de soirée pour prendre l'apéro, on a bien du attendre 10 minutes avant d'avoir les cartes. Ensuite, on passe notre commande (2 bouteilles de vin et des onion rings ac des nachos au guacamole), on ns dit que la cuisine n'est pas encore prête à servir du chaud (il était déjà 18h30, donc un peu étonnant) mais finalement au bout de 5 min on nous dit que cela est possible. La commande passée, on doit patienter encore un bon quart d'heure en voyant nos bouteilles trôner sur le bar, et un des serveurs nous regardant patienter en buvant son propre jus d'orange (tout à fait logique) Quand un serveur se décide enfin à nous servir le tout, on nous sert les nachos avec du cheddar et non du guacamole, on prévient le serveur de l'erreur, il nous dit qu'il n'y a plus de guacamole et qu'il reste que du cheddar fondu (très étonnés que l'on nous sert ce substitut sans notre avis) On fait revenir l'assiette et on entend un autre serveur dire : "Ah ils ne veulent pas du cheddar, oh les relous" Le comble du service.. D'ailleurs 5 min après nous voyons cette même assiette aller sur une table voisine. Plus tard, dans la soirée, je m'aventure sans conviction à commander une assiette de frites, le serveur souriant me dit aucun problème, 20 minutes plus tard, toujours pas de frites et les cuisiniers préparaient déja leur commande du lendemain. Je me relève pour les réclamer de nouveau, le serveur avait l'air complètement dépassé et ne savait pas où ça en était. 20 min plus tard toujours pas de frites. Nous réclamons l'addition. Quelle fût notre surprise de voir les frites facturées alors qu'on a seulement eu le privilège d'en sentir l'odeur mais de ne pas les goûter. Le serveur qui ns apporte l'addition semblait étonné du retard des frites, et comptait nous les apporter mais que l'on a poliment refusé. Une fois les frites annulées, nous avons pu quitter cet endroit pas très chaleureux par l'accueil du personnel, le service et le professionnalisme de celui-ci. Bon point : La location, le décor, les Onion Rings étaient pas mal. Mauvais point : LE SERVICE dans sa globalité, bien dommage.

I stayed at a hotel nearby and went to the no stress cafe on August 4th at 4pm. I speak good French and am British, but was with my American travel companion and so we spoke English together. It became very apparent that our waitress did not like Americans and she decided to take out her aggression with us by being extremely rude and then going to her friend sat at a table behind us and speaking about us to them. I unfortunately could understand everything she said - it was awful - but to be honest she was so aggressive to us that we decided to say nothing so as not to create an incident. She then decided to over charge us 2 euro for each of our drinks. On the menu they were 5 euro each but she put them in as 7 euro. At this point we wanted to leave as soon as possible and so paid the bill with a 10 centime tip and ran - we figured she got her 4 euro service charge by over charging us. Dear No Stress Cafe - if you don't like English speakers - put it on the window - we won't bother you with our custom and drop the English business name - it gives the impression you like us! Also your name is contrary to the Trades Description Act - most hostile and stressful cafe experience EVER!

Le « 138 » (rue du Faubourg Saint-Antoine) est un bar discret à quelques pas de Bastille, et un bon plan pour prendre un dernier verre après 2h sans devoir crier dans l'oreille de son voisin pour discuter, comme dans ces clubs à la musique trop forte. Le 138 est un vaste bar confortable à la lumière tamisée, au fond musical rock bien choisi et à la déco shabby chic faussement négligée. Quelques meubles vaguement baroques, des canapés en cuir capitonné dépareillés invitent à s'affaler à n'importe quelle heure du jour et de la nuit. A l'entrée, un grand comptoir s'ouvre sur une salle tout en longueur, aux baies vitrées lumineuses en journée. Deux autres petites pièces en enfilade avec d'autres canapés mènent à un escalier puis à la cave où vous pouvez faire un dernier tour de piste de danse. En plus, le personnel est sympa et les cuisines sont ouvertes à toute heure pour préparer quelques plats simples (croque-monsieur, salade, tartines). Une carte de cocktails et de vins honnête et quelques bières bouteilles changeront les blasés du demi-pression, les prix restent raisonnables même s'ils sont majorés la nuit. Happy-hour jusqu'à 21h.Auteur : Camille Griffoulières

DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME The waiters are @- holes and will treat you like trash (and steal from you by overcharging). The other staff was really nice, but in France, the waiter runs the show. We had been travelling all day from Italy to Paris, got checked into our hotel and it was 9pm. We were starving (we are vegan so harder to eat on the road), and Al Ajami is on the corner next to our hotel. We came in and asked for an English menu. The hostess was very nice and was very got us a menu we could read. I am better at Italian than French, and needed a little help. Our first time in France, we knew enough to be polite and ask very nicely in french if they would switch to english. Once we were seated, our server ignored us for over 25 minutes. We would have left right then but we were starving and it was late and we didn't want to chance it. The server refused to even look at us. One of the bussers noticed us being ignored and took pity on us and brought us some radishes and olives. Finally the waiter came, and I asked if he would be able to help us in english (I asked in French). He said NO ONLY FRENCH. I said ok and we attempted to order. He was very rude, and then repeated all of our orders back in english (showing that he knew english but choose to not be very nice and force us to try to talk directly to him in French only). Needless to say the food was good, and we ate it all since we were starving. The waiter never came back the entire meal, even though we actually wanted to order more food. I finally asked for the check. When it came, he had charged us 9 Euro for one bottle of water. The hostess even questioned the amount of the water charge, and he told her to bring the check anyways. I could tell she knew we were getting screwed and was uncomfortable with what was happening, but she did as she was told. All in all, very unfriendly. I would eat there again and likely every day of the trip, but they won't get another euro from me because of the attitude and the blatant overcharge.

I just got off the phone with a single female friend who is in Paris for two weeks on business. She has been hiding in the hotel in the evenings after bad experiences as a woman out alone. She called me to see if I could recommend someplace where she could have a good meal, a few drinks and spend the evening in good company. I recommended Le Comete. Last year, my wife and I had a nearby flat for 10 days and by the 4th day, we were eating 2-3 meals per day at Le Comete. Alex and Laura were the most gracious hosts you can imagine and our last evening there turned into a Bon Voyage party. We thought the clientele was mostly local, and they are during the day, but the "regulars" come from all over Paris to spend their evenings in this very special place. One of our favorite memories is Alex leading half the bar in a enthusiastic sing along of Bye Bye American Pie.

I love this place. We have eaten here 3 times. So I told the owner how disappointed I was not to be able to eat the best crepes in Paris on my birthday and she seated us at 10:00. No one else was allowed to come in. When I asked for l'addition, it was on the house.

Being a Breton, I found the place a bit deceptive compared to the reviews. The staff is constantly rushing because of the line outside, but they are very attentive and you never wait too long. The decor is food and fits nicely the place. But I found the food way under my expectations. The galettes were too dry and the crepes were lacking butter. This is because they warm them up instead of making them directly (you can see it even from the outside). Also for my banana - chocolate crepe, it was not real melted chocolate but only some liquid chocolate warmed at the last minute. And finally the cider from the pitcher was not as "brut" and as tasty as I like it, being the kind you find in any grocery store. Good but not great.

If you only hit one creperie in Paris, I highly recommend this one. Be aware that the flambe crepes may have a bit more alcohol than you expect. My favourite crepe is the one with toffee and almonds. Expect a line as this is one of the few Zagat rated creperies on the crepe strip.

J'y ai mangé l'un des pires sandwichs de ma vie ! Un truc fait de pain mou et de rillette infecte : je l'ai mangé jusqu'au bout, mais c'est vraiment parce que j'avais très faim ! Ce lieu à la déco typiquement bobo (vieux exemplaires de boites de produits consommables vendues dans les épiceries françaises dans les années 50 et 60 dans les coins, des motifs à carreaux rouge et blanc, comme les serviettes de troquets d'antan, sur les murs et tables) attire une clientèle de cadres, notamment ceux qui travaillent chez Natixis, quai d'Austerlitz, le midi, et d'habitants du quartier le reste du temps. Tout pour plaire aux nouveaux parigots, mais la qualité des sandwichs n'a rien de traditionnel, ou de conforme au "bon goût d'antant", avant l'époque du speed-fooding. Je ne conseille pas, personnellement.

Comme son nom ne l'indique pas, poissons, coquillages et crustacés sont les spécialités du Café Prunier, petit frère du restaurant Prunier. La maison produit aussi son propre caviar français, pour les amateurs. L'entrée ne paye pas de mine, le décor n'est pas intéressant et notre table n'était pas très bien placée. Qu'importe, l'assiette a fait vibrer nos papilles, le Sauternes recommandé par le garçon était doux au palais et s'est parfaitement marié à une salade tiède de homard à l'huile de noix et piment d'Espelette (35 €). En dessert, on s'est laissé tenter par les trois petits pots de crème Emile Prunier (12 €) moelleux et fondants en bouche. La maison propose un menu entrée-plat-dessert à 40 € et un menu autour de la Saint-Jacques à 95 €. Idéal pour les repas d'affaires. Service impeccable.
